description: Wi-Fi 7 ceiling access point with five radios, one of them an AI radio. Ports: a 10GbE PoE-in port, and a second 10GbE RJ45 shared with a 10GbE SFP+ cage. A GbE RJ45 hands on 48 V PoE. There are also an RJ45 console port, a DC input and a USB 3.0 Type-A port. It carries Bluetooth 5.3. The ports are on the mounting side. The face is a rounded square, smaller than the back, with diagonal ridges, a Wi-Fi mark and wordmark, and one slanted status lamp.

name: ipc-apwf7-poe-cl

chassis.note: datasheet page 3, Dimensions: 9.65 x 9.65 x 2.64 in (245 x 245 x 67 mm), weight 4.41 lb (2.0 kg). `ceiling`: the datasheet says to install it on the ceiling of high-density space. The face is the dome that shows below the ceiling; the rear is the mounting side that carries the ports.

chassis-colour.note: the median of the plain lit face in the stock photograph, #f9f9f8 (69000 pixels); the shaded sides read #e3e3e3 to #ebebeb, which is the lighting and not the plastic.

chassis-shape.note: the datasheet's page 4 figure prints only the three overall dimensions (9.65, 9.65 and 2.64 in) and no corner radius or taper angle. Read off the stock photograph of the face (about 0.17 mm per pixel from the 245 mm width): the plan corner radius is about 43 mm, where the straight edge ends 250 pixels from the corner. A lighter band about 5 mm wide runs along the bottom edge of the face and its lower right, which is the wall seen leaning out, so the face is drawn 5 mm smaller on each side than the back. How deep the taper runs is not shown: it is drawn over the front 25 mm of the 67, which clears the USB-A port, about 11 degrees. The body is built as a taper over a rounded square, in eight chords a corner.

front-layout.note: stock photograph of the face (about 0.17 mm per pixel from the 245 mm width): the wordmark ReadyLinks at the top right with a three-arc Wi-Fi mark above its right-hand letters, five diagonal ridges across the middle, and one status lamp at the bottom left, a bar about 15 mm long slanted at 45 degrees. The wordmark is printed as text, not as the maker's logo; the ridges are drawn as shading and not built up, because no document gives their height. The datasheet does not say what the lamp shows.

power.note: datasheet page 3, Power input: 54 V DC / 1.25 A over a DC connector (2.5 mm inner, 5.5 mm outer), or PoE input over WAN 1 from a PSE that 'complies with IEEE 802.3at/bt standard (PoE+/PoE++)'; 'if both DC power and PoE are available, DC power is preferred'; voltage range PoE mode 'PoE+: 50-57V'. 'PoE interfaces: (1) PoE IN. PoE+/PoE++ IEEE 802.3at/bt'. Max power consumption '60W (Excluding PoE output)', with 'LAN1 for PoE power supply (48 V/12.95 W)' and 'USB port for external power supply (5 V/5 W)' listed among the conditions. So `power-self-max-w` is 60 as printed, `poe-budget-w` is 12.95 (LAN 1), and `poe-pd-max-w` is their sum, 72.95 W. The sheet prints no separate PoE-input figure, does not say whether the 5 W the USB port can supply is inside the 60 W, does not say what the unit does on 802.3at, and prints no 802.3 class. Whether 72.95 W is within what an 802.3bt powered device may take in is not checked: IEEE 802.3 is not held.

rear-layout.note: datasheet page 4, the back view and its callouts: a recessed panel carrying one strip of six ports, legends DC 54V, SFP+, WAN 1/10G/PoE, WAN 2/10G, LAN 1/IoT and Console, in that order left to right. The positions are measured off the figure by scaling its 245 mm body (about 0.52 mm per pixel at 300 dpi); the legends above LAN 1 carry a rating the figure is too small to read and it is not transcribed. The four mounting screws round the panel and the fin pattern are not drawn as parts.

right-layout.note: datasheet page 4, the face view: a USB-A opening on the right-hand edge at about mid-height ('(1) USB 3.0 (Type-A connector)'). Its height along the edge is read from that figure; its depth position in the 67 mm thickness is not shown and is drawn at the middle.

sources.note: ReadyLinks, IPC-APWF7-POE-CL Wi-Fi 7 Ceiling Access Point product datasheet (July 2026, 4 pages): page 3 for the dimensions, ports and power, page 4 for the ports and dimensions figure. The vendor's stock photograph of the face confirms the wordmark and the status lamp. No vendor 3D model and no mechanical drawing is held for this unit.
